question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option "No error".**

And it just recently awarded/ a million-dollar contract/ that reeks of corruption.
solution:
Here the correct answer is **No error.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is** grammatically correct.**
 
• There is no error in any segment of the sentence. 
 
• The sentence is in the **simple past tense**, and all the words are used correctly in their respective places.
 
• The subject** "it"** is followed by the verb **"awarded" **in the past tense, and the object** "a million-dollar contract"** is placed correctly after the verb.
 
• The relative pronoun** "that"** is used correctly to introduce the subordinate clause **"that reeks of corruption."**
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is** option 4, "No error."**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] Confusion Points__**

 
• ​The use of "just" with "recently" is correct and commonly used in English.
 
• **The word "just" is an adverb that indicates a short time ago or a moment ago, while "recently" is an adverb that refers to a time in the near past. When used together, they emphasize the immediacy or freshness of an event or action.**
 
• Here's an example sentence: "I just recently finished reading that book."
 
 
• **In this sentence, the use of "just" emphasizes that the completion of reading the book occurred very recently.**
